events.body:
C1: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (charged $53.17 on a meter with base $3.90, distance $34.84 for 24.7 km, time $12.96 for 49.8 min), so excess kilometres driven pass directly into the fare and are refundable under RD-2. [F6] [RD-2]
C2: The GPS track shows the driver clocked 24.7 km against an optimal 21.6 km, i.e. +3.2 km (+15%) more than needed, and the excess distance was billed at $4.45 (3.2 km × $1.41/km). [F1 F4] [RD-1 RD-2]
C3: One off-route segment between 09:32 and 09:38 added 2.96 km that the optimal route does not need at all (optimal covers 0.00 km there, driver wandered up to 974 m off route); no exemption applies to it, so it is an unexempted detour segment under RD-1. [F3] [RD-1]
C4: The driver never sought the rider's agreement: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all between rider and driver, so there is no rider consent message predating the 09:32 detour start as RD-5 requires. [F7] [RD-5]
C5: The driver's post-trip claim that he 'followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a mere statement with no supporting traffic record, and the traffic data shows no incident near the route in the trip window (only speed band 4, 30–39 km/h, on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) — band 4 is far from the band 1/2 congestion RD-4 requires, and RD-4(b) cannot justify a reroute on its own. [F8 F9 F10 F11 F12] [RD-4]
C6: Refund quantum: the unexempted segment added 2.96 km at the trip's own per-km rate ($34.84 ÷ 24.7 km = $1.4105/km), = $4.18 (rounded to the cent); the small residual difference between the billed 3.2 km and 2.96 km (map-matching residue of ~0.24 km) is not claimed, per RD-2. [F1 F3 F4 F6] [RD-2]
C7: The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes with 1 upheld and 968 trips, and this established route violation makes the pattern repeated, supporting an additional account-review referral; this profile fact is offered only as support for that flag, not as the ground of liability. [F14] [RD-6]

Asks: refund_partial $4.18

The GPS track shows the driver clocked 24.7 km against an optimal 21.6 km, i.e. +3.2 km (+15%) more than needed, and the excess distance was billed at $4.45 (3.2 km × $1.41/km).

One off-route segment between 09:32 and 09:38 added 2.96 km that the optimal route does not need at all (optimal covers 0.00 km there, driver wandered up to 974 m off route); no exemption applies to it, so it is an unexempted detour segment under RD-1.

The driver never sought the rider's agreement: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all between rider and driver, so there is no rider consent message predating the 09:32 detour start as RD-5 requires.

The driver's post-trip claim that he 'followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a mere statement with no supporting traffic record, and the traffic data shows no incident near the route in the trip window (only speed band 4, 30–39 km/h, on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) — band 4 is far from the band 1/2 congestion RD-4 requires, and RD-4(b) cannot justify a reroute on its own.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes with 1 upheld and 968 trips, and this established route violation makes the pattern repeated, supporting an additional account-review referral; this profile fact is offered only as support for that flag, not as the ground of liability.

weaknesses: The trip took 49.8 min against a 28 min estimate (F2) and the fare's time component is $12.96; the driver will argue the extra time and distance were unavoidable on a congested corridor (F9, F10 — East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard both band 4 during 08:58–10:01), though RD-4 requires a recorded incident and RD-4(b) alone cannot exempt a segment.

claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (charged $53.17 on a meter with base $3.90, distance $34.84 for 24.7 km, time $12.96 for 49.8 min), so excess kilometres driven pass directly into the fare and are refundable under RD-2.
The GPS track shows the driver clocked 24.7 km against an optimal 21.6 km, i.e. +3.2 km (+15%) more than needed, and the excess distance was billed at $4.45 (3.2 km × $1.41/km).

One off-route segment between 09:32 and 09:38 added 2.96 km that the optimal route does not need at all (optimal covers 0.00 km there, driver wandered up to 974 m off route); no exemption applies to it, so it is an unexempted detour segment under RD-1.

The driver never sought the rider's agreement: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all between rider and driver, so there is no rider consent message predating the 09:32 detour start as RD-5 requires.

The driver's post-trip claim that he 'followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a mere statement with no supporting traffic record, and the traffic data shows no incident near the route in the trip window (only speed band 4, 30–39 km/h, on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) — band 4 is far from the band 1/2 congestion RD-4 requires, and RD-4(b) cannot justify a reroute on its own.

Refund quantum: the unexempted segment added 2.96 km at the trip's own per-km rate ($34.84 ÷ 24.7 km = $1.4105/km), = $4.18 (rounded to the cent); the small residual difference between the billed 3.2 km and 2.96 km (map-matching residue of ~0.24 km) is not claimed, per RD-2.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes with 1 upheld and 968 trips, and this established route violation makes the pattern repeated, supporting an additional account-review referral; this profile fact is offered only as support for that flag, not as the ground of liability.

weaknesses: The trip took 49.8 min against a 28 min estimate (F2) and the fare's time component is $12.96; the driver will argue the extra time and distance were unavoidable on a congested corridor (F9, F10 — East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard both band 4 during 08:58–10:01), though RD-4 requires a recorded incident and RD-4(b) alone cannot exempt a segment.

There is no chat record at all (F7), so we cannot show the rider affirmatively refused or objected during the trip; the judge may note the absence of consent evidence cuts both ways, and the driver's 'GPS rerouted me' statement (F8) will be used to argue the detour was involuntary, even though a statement cannot beat the GPS record (F3).

The refund we can claim is limited: of the +3.2 km billed (F1, F4) only the 2.96 km off-route segment is a citable unexempted detour (F3), so the claimed amount is $4.18, not the full $4.45 excess billed, and the fare's time component is not refundable under RD-2.

claims.assertion: The total overrun above the optimal route is only +3.2 km (F1), and the disputed off-route segment accounts for 2.96 km of that (F3); the remaining ~0.24 km is map-matching residue, not billable detour under RD-2.

The driver's own GPS rerouting (F8) is not a justified cause for the deviation under RD-4, because the only traffic evidence is speed band 4 (30–39 km/h), which is neither a qualified incident nor band 1/2 congestion (F9, F10), and no incident was recorded near the route (F11); therefore the 2.96 km segment at F3 is an unexempted off-route segment.

There is no in-app chat record of any rider route request, stop, or agreement (F7), so RD-3 and RD-5 give no exemption: neither rider-named stop nor rider consent before the segment's 09:32 start exists (F3).

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F6 meter breakdown: distance $34.84 over 24.7 km = $1.41/km; time $12.96 over 49.8 min), so the refund is limited to the mileage actually added by the unexempted segment: 2.96 km × $1.41 = $4.17, rounded to the cent, per RD-2; no time or waiting units are refundable (waiting $0.00, F6).

The rider's own complaint quoted the excess as 25.0 km vs 22 km (≈3.0 km) and the fare record confirms the billed excess of 3.2 km at $4.45 (F4), so the disputed sum is already bounded by the excess-distance line item and only the 2.96 km segment inside it is refundable.

The driver has 968 trips in 90 days and 1 upheld dispute in 90 days (F14), of which route disputes are 0 (F14), so the profile shows no repeated route violation and RD-6's 'repeated' threshold (≥1 prior upheld route dispute) is not met here.

weaknesses: The GPS record F3 shows a 2.96 km off-route segment reaching up to 974 m from the optimal route between 09:32 and 09:38 — the rider will rely on this as the core of the RD-1 breach.

There is no chat at all (F7): the driver cannot produce any rider message of consent or any stop request, so RD-5 cannot exempt the segment and the driver's statement F8 ('I followed my GPS') is a bare claim that system records contradict.

Traffic facts F9/F10 show band 4 (30–39 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard during the trip window — the rider may present the 49.8 min actual against the 28 min estimate (F2) as corroboration that the route was poor, even though RD-4(b) allows band 1/2 only as corroboration and MVP does not exempt on bands alone.

The driver's profile F14 shows 2 disputes with 1 upheld in 90 days; although route-upheld is 0, the rider can cite it to invite a flag_account request under RD-6 if the judge treats the generic upheld count as relevant.

points.response: Agreed on the arithmetic frame: of the +3.2 km overrun the off-route segment is 2.96 km (F3) and the ~0.24 km residue is map-matching residue that RD-2 expressly leaves with the rider — my brief already claims only the segment km, not the full billed excess.

Conceded and it is decisive: the driver's 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' statement (F8) cannot exempt the segment because RD-4 requires a DataMall incident on the displaced optimal route (F11 shows none) and RD-4(b) bars exemption on bands alone — and the bands here are only 4 (F9, F10), nowhere near band 1/2.

Agreed: the chat record is empty (F7), so the driver has no rider message naming a stop (RD-3) and no consent message timestamped before the 09:32 segment start (RD-5); the segment therefore stands unexempted.

Conceded in substance but corrected on the rate: the trip's own rate is $34.84 ÷ 24.7 km = $1.4105/km (F6), so 2.96 km yields $4.18 rounded to the cent, not $4.17 — the driver's own theory supports refund_partial of $4.18 with no time or waiting units (waiting $0.00, F6).

Accepted that the disputed sum is bounded by the billed excess-distance line of 3.2 km / $4.45 (F4), and my claim remains the 2.96 km segment inside it (F3); note the rider's complaint figure of ~25 km vs 22 km is a lay estimate and the system records F1/F6 govern.

This one I contest only as to outcome, and I do not press the flag: the profile shows route-upheld 0 for this driver (F14), so I withdraw C7 and ask only for the RD-2 refund — the finding of the RD-1 breach itself still stands on F3 and is recorded regardless of the flag.
Withdrawn: on the profile as recorded, 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days (F14), the RD-6 'repeated' threshold is not met, so no flag_account is requested on this record.

Conceded in substance: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so mileage is billable and excess kilometres do enter the fare (F6) — that is exactly why we accept a mileage-only refund under RD-2 rather than resist liability altogether.

Accepted, with the corollary that RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km, not the whole +3.2 km / $4.45 excess line: the 2.96 km at F3 is the refundable measure and the rider himself concedes the ~0.24 km residual is not claimed.
Agreed — the 09:32–09:38 segment is unexempted: no rider-named stop and no consent message precede it (F7), so RD-3 and RD-5 give the driver nothing, and F3 stands as the refundable distance.

Agreed on liability, but the absence of chat cuts against the rider's suggested inference of entitlement beyond the segment: with no recorded route request at all (F7), nothing extends the refundable distance past the single 2.96 km off-route segment (F3).

Agreed: band 4 (30–39 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard is not a qualified incident and not band 1/2 (F9, F10, F11), and RD-4(b) cannot exempt on a band alone, so the driver's statement at F8 cannot beat the GPS record.

The quantum differs by one cent only and both are computable under RD-2: the trip's own meter rate is $34.84 ÷ 24.7 km = $1.410526/km (F6), which times 2.96 km (F3) rounds to $4.18, so we do not contest $4.18 as the cap — both figures sit inside the $4.45 actually billed (F4).

RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and the driver's 90-day route-upheld count is 0 (F14) — this case is the first, so it cannot make the conduct 'repeated' and no flag_account follows; a generic 1-of-2 upheld disputes figure (F14) is not the RD-6 trigger.

notices.text: We reviewed your fare dispute and you're getting $4.18 back. The GPS record showed a stretch of your trip where the driver went 2.96 km off the best route, and you never agreed to that route in the app. On a metered taxi trip, extra distance on a detour like that is refundable, so we calculated it at your trip's own per-kilometre rate. The $4.18 comes to you as a Ryde voucher. The rest of your fare stands, including the small difference on the excess-distance line and all time and waiting charges. No further action is needed from you.
